fixture_metadata.spot_check_status: MEDIUM confidence per Andrew session-44 spot-check; corrections applied: insurer_name split into verbatim/canonical, actuarial_value_source flag added, in_coinsurance_default_post_deductible_only flag added (HDHP semantic clarity), address_line_2 corrected to formal organizational name. Schema gaps documented for Phase 2 §10: cost_cap_per_unit, multi-tier networks, covered_in_network_only discriminator, coverage_conditions verbatim qualifiers for Other Covered services (medically necessary etc), actuarial_value_empirical (v1.5+ from billing data), appeals_contacts multi-entry array.
notes: Insurer mapping: SBC header reads 'Health Net of CA: Bronze 60 HDHP Ambetter PPO'. Health Net of California is the legal entity, Ambetter is Centene's marketplace brand, Centene is the parent. Parser regex /centene|ambetter|wellcare/ maps to 'Centene' — this fixture annotates `insurer_name = Centene` to match parser output and `insurer_brand_name` for the human-readable brand.

Parser fix #1 (this PR): 'No charge after deductible has been met' previously hit the /no\s+charge/ branch in sbc-parser.ts and returned deductibleApplies=false before reaching the /after.*deductible/ check. Fix added a deductible-qualifier check inside the no-charge branch. This fixture's `in_deductible_applies: true` ground truth on post-deductible services validates the fix.

Parser fix #2 (this PR): Coverage Period regex required 'MM/DD/YYYY - MM/DD/YYYY' range. SBC says 'Beginning on or after 01/01/2024' (single date). Parser would have set coverage_period_start, coverage_period_end, AND plan_year to null. Fix added a fallback regex matching 'Beginning On or After MM/DD/YYYY' and assuming calendar-year coverage.

Parser fix #3 (this PR): Coverage tier regex looked for 'individual' / 'family'. SBC says 'All Covered Members' (Ambetter / Health Net) — would have set null. Fix extended the regex to map 'All Covered Members' AND 'Self + Family' (WHA) to 'individual_family'.

Parser fix #4 (this PR): SUD parity derivation. SBCs frequently bundle substance use disorders into mental health rows (page 4 section header 'If you need mental health, behavioral health, or substance abuse services'; ER row says 'Medical, mental health and substance use disorders'). Service catalog has separate substance_abuse_outpatient/inpatient slugs but the parser previously emitted only mental_health_*. Fix added a post-process step: when the SBC text contains /substance\s+(?:abuse|use)/, mirror each mental_health_outpatient/inpatient entry into a substance_abuse_* counterpart with identical cost-sharing. ACA mental health parity laws require SUD coverage at parity with mental health, so the values match. The parser emits a parseWarning when derivation runs so audit reviewers can see ground truth was synthesized rather than extracted.

Slug added (this PR): 'routine_eye_exam_adult' added to service_catalog (TypeScript seed + migration 054). Adult routine eye care appears in 'Other Covered Services' on this SBC; without this slug the coverage was silently dropped. Existing slugs 'abortion' and 'bariatric_surgery' were already present — they're now annotated below.

Prior authorization conventions: `prior_auth_required: true` means PA can apply. The verbatim qualifier (e.g. 'Some outpatient surgical procedures require PA', 'Required for non-emergency only', 'Required for services other than office visits', 'Required for select drugs') is captured EXACTLY in `coverage_conditions`. No separate prior_auth_scope enum — the verbatim text is the source of truth, since coarse buckets like 'some' lose the operationally important distinction between 'non-emergency only' / 'non-office only' / 'select drugs' / etc.

Cost-sharing for 'Other Covered Services' (acupuncture, bariatric_surgery, routine_eye_exam_adult): SBC explicitly states these are covered but does NOT state cost-sharing. Per accuracy-above-all-else principle, cost fields are `null` (not inferred from the plan's general pattern) — the EOC is the authoritative source. Coverage_conditions captures the verbatim 'Other Covered Services' text. Abortion is the EXCEPTION because the SBC explicitly says 'covered in full', which is a cost-sharing statement (= $0 cost-share, deductible does not apply).

Inferred fields (NOT explicit in SBC text): hsa_eligible (derived from HDHP + IRS 2024 limits — plan deductible $7,050 ≥ $1,600 min, OOP $7,050 ≤ $8,050 max — fixture-only field, not in InsurancePlanRow yet), in_coinsurance_default: 0 (HDHP semantics — post-deductible cost-share is zero), combined_medical_rx_oop: true (no separate Rx OOP listed), actuarial_value: 0.60 (Bronze 60 plan name).

Schema gap (not closed in this PR): hsa_eligible, metal_level, actuarial_value, csr_level, is_hdhp, marketplace_type, on_marketplace, hios_id, insurer_brand_name are fixture-only annotation fields. They are not columns on insurance_plans yet. Adding them is a Phase 4/5 schema migration and out of scope for 1C.1.

HDHP signature: in_oop_max_individual ($7,050) equals in_deductible_individual ($7,050). Once the deductible is met, the plan covers everything in-network. This is correct HDHP design, not a data error.
MVS = 'Not Applicable' on the SBC. MVS is an employer-plan concept; individual marketplace plans are not subject to the standard. Annotated as `null` (= not applicable), not `false`.

Home health visit limit ambiguity: SBC says 'Limited to 100 visits per calendar year (rehabilitative and habilitative home health services are each limited to separate 100 visit limits each calendar year).' Could mean total 100 with sub-limits OR 100 + 100 + 100 = 300 max. Annotated as 100 headline cap; verbatim text preserved in coverage_conditions.
